gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the '130W' on the UGREEN Nexode 20,000 mAh 130W, ChatGPT's 'pick for most people', is 100 W from USB-C1 plus at most 30 W from USB-C2. The Anker Prime 26K's '300W' is 140 W from each USB-C port. So the UGREEN cannot charge a laptop and a 45 W phone at full speed together. UGREEN also rates a 20,000 mAh sister model at only 11,300 mAh at 5 V, and Anker says the 26,250 mAh Prime delivers about 15,200 mAh.
standout_why: I compared against three cited pages. Popular Science (cited in 6 of 7 chats, updated 2026-10-26) gives the UGREEN Nexode 20K only as '130W total output, per UGREEN' and says 'No per-port breakdown is listed'. It explains mAh vs Wh in general but gives no usable or rated capacity for any pick. Wirecutter (via the proxy URL, cited) gives the Prime as '140 W apiece' and '300 W total' but has no usable-capacity figure and does not cover the UGREEN 130W. Expert Reviews (cited, updated 2026-11-11) confirms the Prime's two USB-C ports give 140 W at once. Its only 20K UGREEN is the PB771, which has a 45 W second port and is not the 130W model. None of them gives the 100 W + 30 W split of the 130W model or any maker's rated capacity at 5 V. I could not open TechRadar, Wired, Android Central (truncated) or thisUSB (certificate error), so I could not compare against those pages.
decides: This confirms the Anker Prime 26K as the only candidate that really charges two laptops, since its 300 W is 140 W + 140 W. It weakens ChatGPT's 'best value' pick for anyone charging a laptop plus a fast phone or tablet. The UGREEN 130W's second USB-C stops at 30 W, so the '130W' only adds up with a 100 W laptop on C1 and a phone that is happy at 30 W on C2. For a laptop plus a 45 W Galaxy, the UGREEN 145W 25K fits better: its second USB-C gives 65 W and its first gives 140 W. The page's footnote should say that the wattage in the name is a sum of port limits, not a speed, and that usable output is about 58–78% of the mAh on the box, by the makers' own figures.
